Anomaly Detection
Select one or more detection methods and configure their parameters.
No data loaded. Go to Upload Data to get started.
Statistical Outlier Detection — values unusual relative to the data's distribution
Statistical Outliers
Flags values that fall beyond a configurable Z-score or IQR threshold — effective for amounts, quantities, or any continuous numeric field
σ / IQR
Duplicate Detection
Identifies exact or near-duplicate rows across selected key fields — useful for double payments, duplicate invoices, or repeated transactions
Date Anomalies
Flags weekend transactions, holiday postings, after-hours timestamps, future dates, or dates outside the audit period
Multivariate / ML Detection — finds rows anomalous across several fields at once JS engine
Isolation Forest
Isolates anomalies by random partitioning — rows separated in few splits are outliers. Strong general-purpose multivariate detector, no distribution assumptions
Mahalanobis Distance
Measures distance from the multivariate centre accounting for correlations between fields. Flags rows far from the joint distribution — assumes roughly elliptical data
Local Outlier Factor (LOF)
Compares each row's local density to its neighbours' — catches anomalies that are only unusual relative to their local cluster, which global methods miss
Fraud Indicator Tests — forensic signatures of manipulation, not statistical outliers
Benford's Law
Tests whether first-digit distributions match the expected logarithmic pattern — highly effective for detecting fabricated or rounded amounts
Round Number Test
Flags values ending in .00, .50, or round thousands — disproportionate rounding can indicate estimates, fabrication, or just-below-threshold splitting
Sequence Gap Analysis
Detects missing numbers in a sequential field such as invoice numbers, check numbers, or purchase order IDs
